name: X-linked cleft palate and ankyloglossia
aliases: X-linked cleft palate and tongue-tie syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnostic criteria for X-linked cleft palate and ankyloglossia

criteria.description: Presence of cleft palate (complete or incomplete)
Congenital ankyloglossia (tongue-tie) with restricted tongue mobility
X-linked inheritance pattern with affected male relatives
Absence of cleft lip differentiating from other cleft syndromes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of cleft palate and ankyloglossia in a male patient with or without supportive family history consistent with X-linked inheritance
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may confirm diagnosis but is not always available.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Isolated cleft palate without cleft lip
pathognomonic.notes: Typically manifests as a midline defect of the secondary palate
searchTerms: split roof of mouth without lip cleft

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital ankyloglossia (tongue-tie) with restricted tongue mobility
pathognomonic.notes: Leads to feeding difficulties and speech impairment

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulties in infancy due to palatal insufficiency
searchTerms: infant feeding problems from palate issues

common.symptomName: Speech articulation disorders related to palatal dysfunction
Recurrent otitis media due to Eustachian tube dysfunction
common.notes: May lead to conductive hearing loss
searchTerms: repeated ear infections from Eustachian tube problems
chronic ear infections due to tube dysfunction

common.symptomName: Delayed tooth eruption or dental anomalies

occasional.notes: Secondary to recurrent middle ear infections

occasional.symptomName: Mild developmental delay in speech and language
occasional.notes: Related to palatal and tongue mobility issues

searchTerms: food or liquid coming out of nose when swallowing

rare.notes: May be present in milder phenotypes
Occult defect of the palate musculature
searchTerms: submucous cleft in roof of mouth

rare.symptomName: Mild conductive hearing impairment requiring intervention
searchTerms: mild hearing loss from middle ear

imaging: Palatal ultrasound or MRI showing cleft palate anatomy
genetic: X-linked inheritance pattern confirmed by family genetic studies
other: Clinical observation of restricted tongue mobility
Feeding assessment revealing difficulties related to palatal defect

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of cleft lip and palate
Cleft lip and/or palate with popliteal webbing

redFlags: Severe feeding difficulties leading to failure to thrive
Recurrent aspiration pneumonia due to palatal insufficiency
Progressive conductive hearing loss impacting speech development
references: Orphanet: X-linked cleft palate and ankyloglossia - ORPHA:324601
Smith et al., Clinical Genetics of Cleft Palate Syndromes, 2022
Jones and Smith, Genetic Disorders of the Palate, 2023
